records.source: וְאֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֥ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה עֶ֣שֶׂר יְרִיעֹ֑ת שֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֗ר וּתְכֵ֤לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן֙ וְתֹלַ֣עַת שָׁנִ֔י כְּרֻבִ֛ים מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֹשֵׁ֖ב תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And the tabernacle you will make [of] ten curtains [of] fine twisted linen and blue and purple and scarlet [yarn]; [with] cherubim, the work of a skillful worker, you will make them.
pieces: For the tabernacle you are to make ten curtains of fine twisted linen and of blue, purple and scarlet yarn. Have cherubim worked into them, the design of a skilled craftsman.

L.1: And the tabernacle you shall make [of] ten curtains of fine twisted linen and blue and purple and scarlet [yarn]; [with] cherubim, the work of a skilled craftsman, you shall make them.

R.1: Make the tabernacle, the sacred tent, out of ten curtains. Make them from fine twisted linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn. Have a skilled craftsman work cherubim into the cloth.

decisions.choice: tabernacle: the dwelling, the tent where God would live among his people
decisions.reason: The word means a dwelling place. God said, "Let them make me a sanctuary, so that I may dwell among them" (25:8), and this word comes from the same root as "dwell". In this chapter it names first the inner layer of linen curtains (verses 1-6) and then the whole structure (verses 15-30).

decisions.choice: fine twisted linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn: the costliest cloth and dyes
decisions.reason: Linen of fine thread, spun from several strands twisted together, was the best cloth of Egypt. Blue and purple dyes, made from sea snails, and scarlet, made from an insect, were rare and costly. The same materials are listed among the gifts in 25:4.

decisions.choice: the work of a skillful worker: woven in a design by a master craftsman
decisions.reason: The worker named here is one who designs and devises (31:4; 35:35). His work is set apart from that of the embroiderer, who makes the screen at the entrance (verse 36). Here the cherubim are woven into the cloth itself.

decisions.choice: the sacred tent
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the sacred tent" to explain "tabernacle", a word many readers do not use.

records.heading: The tabernacle curtains

records.source: אֹ֣רֶךְ׀הַיְרִיעָ֣ה הָֽאַחַ֗ת שְׁמֹנֶ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙ בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה וְרֹ֨חַב֙ אַרְבַּ֣ע בָּאַמָּ֔ה הַיְרִיעָ֖ה הָאֶחָ֑ת מִדָּ֥ה אַחַ֖ת לְכָל־הַיְרִיעֹֽת׃
records.gloss: The length of the one curtain [will be] eight and twenty by the cubit, and the width four by the cubit, the one curtain; one measure for all the curtains.
pieces: Each curtain is to be {{units:about 42 feet|28 cubits}} long and {{units:about 6 feet|4 cubits}} wide; all the curtains are to have one measure.

L.2: The length of the one curtain [shall be] 28 cubits, and the width of the one curtain 4 cubits; one measure for all the curtains.

R.2: Each curtain must be {{units:about 42 feet|28 cubits}} long and {{units:about 6 feet|4 cubits}} wide. Make them all the same size.

decisions.choice: cubit: the length from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger, about 18 inches
decisions.reason: The cubit was the common measure of length. It was about 18 inches (about 45 centimeters); a longer royal cubit was also known (Ezekiel 40:5). So each linen curtain was about 42 feet long and 6 feet wide.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 42 feet|28 cubits}}
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the measure in feet and inches, taking a cubit as about 18 inches; the setting shows the cubits of the Hebrew. Literal keeps the cubits.

records.source: חֲמֵ֣שׁ הַיְרִיעֹ֗ת תִּֽהְיֶ֨יןָ֙ חֹֽבְרֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל־אֲחֹתָ֑הּ וְחָמֵ֤שׁ יְרִיעֹת֙ חֹֽבְרֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל־אֲחֹתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Five of the curtains will be joined, a woman to her sister, and five curtains joined, a woman to her sister.
pieces: Five of the curtains are to be joined to one another, and the other five joined to one another as well.

L.3: Five of the curtains shall be joined one to another, and five curtains joined one to another.

R.3: Join five of the curtains together into one set. Do the same with the other five.

decisions.choice: a woman to her sister: one to another
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "a woman to her sister", a way of saying "each to the other" when the nouns are feminine, as "curtain" is. The same phrase returns in verses 5, 6 and 17. The ten curtains form two sets of five.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֜יתָ לֻֽלְאֹ֣ת תְּכֵ֗לֶת עַ֣ל שְׂפַ֤ת הַיְרִיעָה֙ הָאֶחָ֔ת מִקָּצָ֖ה בַּחֹבָ֑רֶת וְכֵ֤ן תַּעֲשֶׂה֙ בִּשְׂפַ֣ת הַיְרִיעָ֔ה הַקִּ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה בַּמַּחְבֶּ֖רֶת הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃
records.gloss: And you will make loops of blue on the edge of the one curtain at the end in the set; and so you will do on the edge of the outermost curtain in the second set.
pieces: Put loops of blue yarn on the outer edge of the last curtain in the first set. Put them likewise on the edge of the outermost curtain of the second set.

L.4: And you shall make loops of blue on the edge of the one curtain, at the end in the set; and so you shall do on the edge of the outermost curtain in the second set.

R.4: Make loops of blue yarn along the edge of the last curtain in each set.

decisions.choice: the set: the group of five joined curtains
decisions.reason: The word means a joining, here the joined group of five curtains (verse 3). The loops go on the edge of the end curtain of each set, where the two sets meet.

decisions.choice: in each set
decisions.reason: Readable says the two halves of the verse once, since the same thing is done to both sets.

records.source: חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻֽלָאֹ֗ת תַּעֲשֶׂה֮ בַּיְרִיעָ֣ה הָאֶחָת֒ וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻֽלָאֹ֗ת תַּעֲשֶׂה֙ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַיְרִיעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בַּמַּחְבֶּ֣רֶת הַשֵּׁנִ֑ית מַקְבִּילֹת֙ הַלֻּ֣לָאֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל־אֲחֹתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Fifty loops you will make on the one curtain, and fifty loops you will make on the end of the curtain which [is] in the second set, the loops opposite, a woman to her sister.
pieces: Put fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty on the end of the curtain in the second set, so that the loops line up with each other.

L.5: Fifty loops you shall make on the one curtain, and fifty loops you shall make on the end of the curtain that [is] in the second set, the loops [being] opposite one another.

R.5: There should be fifty loops on each of these two curtains, and the loops should line up across from each other.

decisions.choice: opposite: facing each other in matching pairs
decisions.reason: The loops on the two edges face each other, so that each pair can be fastened with one clasp (verse 6).

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֕יתָ חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים קַרְסֵ֣י זָהָ֑ב וְחִבַּרְתָּ֨אֶת־הַיְרִיעֹ֜ת אִשָּׁ֤ה אֶל־אֲחֹתָהּ֙ בַּקְּרָסִ֔ים וְהָיָ֥ה הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן אֶחָֽד׃פ
records.gloss: And you will make fifty clasps of gold and join the curtains, a woman to her sister, with the clasps, and the tabernacle will be one.
pieces: Make fifty clasps of gold and join the two sets of curtains with them, one to the other. Then the tabernacle will be one whole.

L.6: And you shall make fifty clasps of gold and join the curtains one to another with the clasps, and the tabernacle shall be one.

R.6: Make fifty gold clasps. Hook the two sets of curtains together with them. Then the tabernacle will be all one piece.

decisions.choice: clasps: fasteners that hook through the loops
decisions.reason: The word is used only of the tabernacle (here, verses 11 and 33; 35:11; 39:33). Each clasp passes through a pair of loops and holds the two sets of curtains together.

decisions.choice: the tabernacle will be one: a single dwelling
decisions.reason: The ten curtains are to become one tabernacle, one dwelling for God among his people. The same words are said of the tent in verse 11.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ֙ יְרִיעֹ֣ת עִזִּ֔ים לְאֹ֖הֶל עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עַשְׁתֵּי־עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה יְרִיעֹ֖ת תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will make curtains of goats' [hair] for a tent over the tabernacle; eleven curtains you will make them.
pieces: Then make eleven curtains of goats' hair to be a tent over the tabernacle.

L.7: And you shall make curtains of goats' [hair] for a tent over the tabernacle; eleven curtains you shall make.

R.7: Make eleven curtains of goats' hair. They will form a tent that covers the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: goats' hair: coarse dark cloth, used for tents
decisions.reason: Cloth woven from the hair of black goats was tough and kept out the rain. It was the usual cloth for tents (compare Song of Songs 1:5). It was among the gifts asked for in 25:4.

decisions.choice: a tent over the tabernacle: a second layer spread above the linen
decisions.reason: Here "the tabernacle" is the layer of linen curtains (verses 1-6), and "the tent" is the layer of goats'-hair curtains spread over it.

records.heading: The tent of goats' hair

records.source: אֹ֣רֶךְ׀הַיְרִיעָ֣ה הָֽאַחַ֗ת שְׁלֹשִׁים֙ בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה וְרֹ֨חַב֙ אַרְבַּ֣ע בָּאַמָּ֔ה הַיְרִיעָ֖ה הָאֶחָ֑ת מִדָּ֣ה אַחַ֔ת לְעַשְׁתֵּ֥י עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה יְרִיעֹֽת׃
records.gloss: The length of the one curtain [will be] thirty by the cubit, and the width four by the cubit, the one curtain; one measure for the eleven curtains.
pieces: Each curtain is to be {{units:about 45 feet|30 cubits}} long and {{units:about 6 feet|4 cubits}} wide; all eleven are to have one measure.

L.8: The length of the one curtain [shall be] 30 cubits, and the width of the one curtain 4 cubits; one measure for the eleven curtains.

R.8: Each of these curtains must be {{units:about 45 feet|30 cubits}} long and {{units:about 6 feet|4 cubits}} wide. All eleven must be the same size.

decisions.choice: thirty cubits: two cubits longer than the linen curtains
decisions.reason: The goats'-hair curtains are longer than the linen ones (28 cubits, verse 2), and there is one more of them, so the outer tent covers the inner one fully (verses 12-13).

decisions.choice: {{units:about 45 feet|30 cubits}}
decisions.reason: Measures as in verse 2, with a cubit as about 18 inches.

records.source: וְחִבַּרְתָּ֞ אֶת־חֲמֵ֤שׁ הַיְרִיעֹת֙ לְבָ֔ד וְאֶת־שֵׁ֥שׁ הַיְרִיעֹ֖ת לְבָ֑ד וְכָפַלְתָּ֙ אֶת־הַיְרִיעָ֣ה הַשִּׁשִּׁ֔ית אֶל־מ֖וּל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֹֽהֶל׃
records.gloss: And you will join five of the curtains by themselves and six of the curtains by themselves, and you will fold double the sixth curtain toward the front of the face of the tent.
pieces: Join five curtains together by themselves, and six by themselves. The sixth curtain is to be folded over double across the front of the tent.

L.9: And you shall join five of the curtains by themselves and six of the curtains by themselves, and you shall fold double the sixth curtain at the front of the tent.

R.9: Join five of them together, and join the other six together. Fold the extra sixth curtain in half and let it hang at the front of the tent.

decisions.choice: fold double the sixth curtain: the extra curtain is doubled over at the entrance
decisions.reason: With six curtains in one set, the goats'-hair tent is one curtain wider than the linen beneath it. Half of the extra width is folded over at the front; the other half hangs at the back (verse 12). Just how the fold lay is not described.

decisions.choice: the extra sixth curtain ... in half ... let it hang
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the sixth curtain is the one more than the linen set has, and what folding it double means.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֜יתָ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻֽלָאֹ֗ת עַ֣ל שְׂפַ֤ת הַיְרִיעָה֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ת הַקִּיצֹנָ֖ה בַּחֹבָ֑רֶת וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים לֻֽלָאֹ֗ת עַ֚ל שְׂפַ֣ת הַיְרִיעָ֔ה הַחֹבֶ֖רֶת הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃
records.gloss: And you will make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain, the outermost in the set, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain [of] the second set.
pieces: On the outer edge of the last curtain in the first set put fifty loops, and fifty more on the edge of the joining curtain in the second set.

L.10: And you shall make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain, the outermost in the set, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain [of] the second set.

R.10: Put fifty loops along the edge of the last curtain in each set.

decisions.choice: fifty loops: the goats'-hair sets are joined as the linen sets were
decisions.reason: The outer tent is joined in the same way as the inner tabernacle (verses 4-5): fifty loops on each edge where the two sets meet.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֛יתָ קַרְסֵ֥י נְחֹ֖שֶׁת חֲמִשִּׁ֑ים וְהֵבֵאתָ֤ אֶת־הַקְּרָסִים֙ בַּלֻּ֣לָאֹ֔ת וְחִבַּרְתָּ֥ אֶת־הָאֹ֖הֶל וְהָיָ֥ה אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And you will make clasps of bronze, fifty, and you will put the clasps in the loops and join together the tent, and it will be one.
pieces: Make fifty clasps of bronze. Fit the clasps into the loops and join the tent together, so that it becomes one whole.

L.11: And you shall make fifty clasps of bronze, and you shall put the clasps into the loops and join the tent together, and it shall be one.

R.11: Make fifty bronze clasps and hook them through the loops. This will join the tent into one piece.

decisions.choice: bronze: a less costly metal for the outer layer
decisions.reason: The clasps of the inner linen layer are gold (verse 6); those of the outer goats'-hair tent are bronze. Throughout the tabernacle the metals are more precious the nearer they are to the most holy place (compare verses 32 and 37).

records.source: וְסֶ֨רַח֙ הָעֹדֵ֔ף בִּירִיעֹ֖ת הָאֹ֑הֶל חֲצִ֤י הַיְרִיעָה֙ הָעֹדֶ֔פֶת תִּסְרַ֕ח עַ֖ל אֲחֹרֵ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן׃
records.gloss: And the overhang of the surplus in the curtains of the tent, the half of the curtain that is surplus, will hang over the rear of the tabernacle.
pieces: Half of a curtain will be left over from the curtains of the tent. Let that surplus hang down over the rear of the tabernacle.

L.12: And the overhanging part that is left over in the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that is left over, shall hang over the back of the tabernacle.

R.12: The goats'-hair curtains cover more than the linen ones. Let the extra half curtain hang down over the back of the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: the half curtain left over: the surplus width at the back
decisions.reason: Eleven goats'-hair curtains, 4 cubits wide, are 44 cubits across; the ten linen curtains are 40. One extra curtain was folded double at the front (verse 9), so half a curtain remains to hang at the rear. The verse does not say exactly how it was arranged.

decisions.choice: The goats'-hair curtains cover more than the linen ones.
decisions.reason: Readable adds a sentence to explain why there is a half curtain left over.

records.source: וְהָאַמָּ֨ה מִזֶּ֜ה וְהָאַמָּ֤ה מִזֶּה֙ בָּעֹדֵ֔ף בְּאֹ֖רֶךְ יְרִיעֹ֣ת הָאֹ֑הֶל יִהְיֶ֨ה סָר֜וּחַ עַל־צִדֵּ֧י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן מִזֶּ֥ה וּמִזֶּ֖ה לְכַסֹּתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And the cubit from this [side] and the cubit from this [side], in the surplus in the length of the curtains of the tent, will be overhanging over the sides of the tabernacle from this and from this, to cover it.
pieces: In length the tent curtains will be longer by {{units:about 18 inches|a cubit}} at each end. Let this surplus hang down over both sides of the tabernacle and cover it.

L.13: And the cubit on this [side] and the cubit on that [side], of what is left over in the length of the curtains of the tent, shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle, on this [side] and on that [side], to cover it.

R.13: The goats'-hair curtains are also longer. Let {{units:about 18 inches|a cubit}} of extra cloth hang down on each side of the tabernacle to cover it.

decisions.choice: the cubit on this side and the cubit on that side: one cubit extra at each side
decisions.reason: The goats'-hair curtains are 30 cubits long (verse 8) and the linen ones 28 (verse 2). The extra two cubits give one cubit more on each side, so the outer tent hangs lower than the linen and covers it.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 18 inches|a cubit}}
decisions.reason: Measures as in verse 2, with a cubit as about 18 inches.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ מִכְסֶה֙ לָאֹ֔הֶל עֹרֹ֥ת אֵילִ֖ם מְאָדָּמִ֑ים וּמִכְסֵ֛ה עֹרֹ֥ת תְּחָשִׁ֖ים מִלְמָֽעְלָה׃פ
records.gloss: And you will make a covering for the tent [of] skins of rams dyed red, and a covering of skins of [tachash] from above.
pieces: Make a covering for the tent out of rams' skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.

L.14: And you shall make a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering of fine leather above [that].

R.14: Make a covering for the tent from rams' skins dyed red. Over that, put a covering of fine leather.

decisions.choice: rams' skins dyed red: tanned leather colored red
decisions.reason: The skins of rams were tanned, and the tanning or a dye gave them a red color. They are among the gifts listed in 25:5.

decisions.choice: fine leather: skins of an animal or leather of a kind no longer known
decisions.reason: The word that names these skins is rare: it is found with the tabernacle (25:5; 35:7; Numbers 4:6-14) and for sandals in Ezekiel 16:10. It has been taken as the name of a sea animal, such as the dolphin or the dugong (sea cow), found in the Red Sea; as a kind of leather of special finish; or as a color. The meaning is not certain.

decisions.choice: from above: the outermost covering
decisions.reason: The phrase places this covering on top. Over the linen tabernacle lies the goats'-hair tent, then the rams' skins, then this covering of leather.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת־הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֲצֵ֥י שִׁטִּ֖ים עֹמְדִֽים׃
records.gloss: And you will make the frames for the tabernacle [of] wood of acacia, standing.
pieces: For the tabernacle make frames out of acacia wood, to stand upright.

L.15: And you shall make the frames for the tabernacle [of] acacia wood, standing [upright].

R.15: Make frames of acacia wood. They will stand up straight and form the walls of the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: frames: open upright frameworks, or perhaps solid boards
decisions.reason: The word is used of these pieces and once of the deck of a ship (Ezekiel 27:6). It has often been taken as solid boards or planks. But boards 10 cubits high and a cubit and a half wide (verse 16) would be very heavy to carry, each one has two "hands" (verse 17), and the cherubim of the linen curtains would be hidden behind a solid wall. So many take each piece as an open frame of two uprights joined by crosspieces. Either way, the pieces stand side by side to form the walls.

decisions.choice: acacia wood: a hard wood of the desert
decisions.reason: The acacia grows in the Sinai desert and the Jordan valley. Its wood is hard, light and lasting. The ark, the table, the altars and the poles were all made of it (25:10, 23; 27:1; 30:1).

decisions.choice: form the walls
decisions.reason: Readable says what the frames are for, which verses 18-25 make plain.

records.heading: The frames

records.source: עֶ֥שֶׂר אַמּ֖וֹת אֹ֣רֶךְ הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ וְאַמָּה֙ וַחֲצִ֣י הָֽאַמָּ֔ה רֹ֖חַב הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: Ten cubits [will be] the length of the frame, and a cubit and the half of the cubit the width of the one frame.
pieces: Make every frame {{units:about 15 feet|10 cubits}} high and {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|a cubit and a half}} wide.

L.16: Ten cubits [shall be] the length of the frame, and a cubit and a half the width of the one frame.

R.16: Each frame must be {{units:about 15 feet|10 cubits}} tall and {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|a cubit and a half}} wide.

decisions.choice: length: the height of the standing frame
decisions.reason: Because the frames stand upright (verse 15), their length is their height. Twenty frames a cubit and a half wide make a wall 30 cubits long (verse 18).

decisions.choice: {{units:about 15 feet|10 cubits}} high; {{units:about 2 1/4 feet|a cubit and a half}} wide
decisions.reason: Measures as in verse 2, with a cubit as about 18 inches. Balanced and Readable say "high" or "tall" for the length of a standing frame.

records.source: שְׁתֵּ֣י יָד֗וֹת לַקֶּ֨רֶשׁ֙ הָאֶחָ֔ד מְשֻׁלָּבֹ֔ת אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶל־אֲחֹתָ֑הּ כֵּ֣ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל קַרְשֵׁ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּֽן׃
records.gloss: Two hands [will be] for the one frame, joined, a woman to her sister; so you will do for all the frames of the tabernacle.
pieces: Every frame will have two tenons, joined one to the other. Do this for every frame of the tabernacle.

L.17: Two tenons [shall be] for the one frame, joined one to another; so you shall do for all the frames of the tabernacle.

R.17: Each frame must have two pegs at the bottom, joined to each other. Make every frame of the tabernacle the same way.

decisions.choice: hands: tenons, pegs that fit into the bases
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "hands". They are the projecting ends of the frame that fit into the two silver bases beneath it (verse 19). They may be the lower ends of the two uprights of an open frame (see verse 15).

decisions.choice: joined to each other: the two tenons are linked together
alternatives: each frame joined to the next
decisions.reason: The word means joined or fitted, like the rungs of a ladder. It may mean the two uprights were joined by crosspieces, or that the tenons were set parallel. Some take it to mean that each frame was joined to the next.

decisions.choice: pegs at the bottom
decisions.reason: Readable says "pegs" for the tenons and adds where they are.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת־הַקְּרָשִׁ֖ים לַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן עֶשְׂרִ֣ים קֶ֔רֶשׁ לִפְאַ֖ת נֶ֥גְבָּה תֵימָֽנָה׃
records.gloss: And you will make the frames for the tabernacle: twenty frames for the side of the Negev, southward.
pieces: The south side of the tabernacle is to have twenty frames.

L.18: And you shall make the frames for the tabernacle: twenty frames for the side toward the Negev, southward.

R.18: Make twenty frames for the south wall of the tabernacle.

decisions.choice: toward the Negev, southward: on the south side
decisions.reason: Two words for "south" stand together. The first is the Negev, the dry land to the south of Canaan; the second means the south. Together they stress the direction. The tabernacle faced east (27:13), so the south side was on the right.

records.source: וְאַרְבָּעִים֙ אַדְנֵי־כֶ֔סֶף תַּעֲשֶׂ֕ה תַּ֖חַת עֶשְׂרִ֣ים הַקָּ֑רֶשׁ שְׁנֵ֨י אֲדָנִ֜ים תַּֽחַת־הַקֶּ֤רֶשׁ הָאֶחָד֙ לִשְׁתֵּ֣י יְדֹתָ֔יו וּשְׁנֵ֧י אֲדָנִ֛ים תַּֽחַת־הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֖ד לִשְׁתֵּ֥י יְדֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And forty bases of silver you will make under the twenty frames: two bases under the one frame for its two hands, and two bases under the one frame for its two hands.
pieces: Under the twenty frames set forty bases of silver, two beneath every frame to receive its two tenons.

L.19: And forty bases of silver you shall make under the twenty frames: two bases under the one frame for its two tenons, and two bases under the one frame for its two tenons.

R.19: Make forty silver bases to set under these twenty frames. Each frame stands in two bases, one for each peg.

decisions.choice: bases: heavy sockets that hold the foot of each frame
decisions.reason: The word means a base or footing (Job 38:6). Each frame stands in two of them. According to 38:25-27 the silver for these bases came from the half shekel each man paid when the people were counted.

decisions.choice: two bases under the one frame, and two under the one frame: two under each frame
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the phrase to mean "under each frame in turn". The same pattern returns in verses 21 and 25.

records.source: וּלְצֶ֧לַע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֛ן הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית לִפְאַ֣ת צָפ֑וֹן עֶשְׂרִ֖ים קָֽרֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And for the second side of the tabernacle, toward the side of the north, twenty frames,
pieces: For the other side of the tabernacle, the north side, make twenty frames

L.20: And for the second side of the tabernacle, toward the north side, twenty frames,

R.20: Make twenty frames for the north wall too.

decisions.choice: side: one of the long sides of the structure
decisions.reason: The word means side, and it is also the word for the rib taken from the man (Genesis 2:21-22). Here it is a long side wall of the tabernacle, as in verses 26-27.

records.source: וְאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אַדְנֵיהֶ֖ם כָּ֑סֶף שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת הַקֶּ֣רֶשׁ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: and their forty bases [of] silver: two bases under the one frame and two bases under the one frame.
pieces: with their forty silver bases, two under each frame.

L.21: and their forty bases [of] silver: two bases under the one frame and two bases under the one frame.

R.21: They also need forty silver bases, two under each frame.

decisions.choice: two bases under each frame
decisions.reason: The repeated phrase means two under each frame, as in verse 19. The north side matches the south.

records.source: וּֽלְיַרְכְּתֵ֥י הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן יָ֑מָּה תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה שִׁשָּׁ֥ה קְרָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And for the far parts of the tabernacle, seaward, you will make six frames.
pieces: For the back of the tabernacle, the west end, make six frames.

L.22: And for the rear of the tabernacle, westward, you shall make six frames.

R.22: Make six frames for the back wall, at the west end.

decisions.choice: seaward: westward
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "toward the sea", that is, toward the Mediterranean, which lies west of Canaan. It is the usual way to say west.

decisions.choice: the far parts: the back of the tabernacle
decisions.reason: The word means the remotest or innermost part. The entrance faced east (verse 36; 27:13), so the back was the west end, where the most holy place stood.

records.source: וּשְׁנֵ֤י קְרָשִׁים֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה לִמְקֻצְעֹ֖ת הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן בַּיַּרְכָתָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And two frames you will make for the corners of the tabernacle in the far parts.
pieces: Two more frames are for the back corners of the tabernacle.

L.23: And two frames you shall make for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear.

R.23: Make two more frames for the back corners.

decisions.choice: corners: the two back corners
decisions.reason: These two frames stand where the back wall meets the side walls. Their shape is not described, beyond what verse 24 says.

records.source: וְיִֽהְי֣וּ תֹֽאֲמִים֮ מִלְּמַטָּה֒ וְיַחְדָּ֗ו יִהְי֤וּ תַמִּים֙ עַל־רֹאשׁ֔וֹ אֶל־הַטַּבַּ֖עַת הָאֶחָ֑ת כֵּ֚ן יִהְיֶ֣ה לִשְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם לִשְׁנֵ֥י הַמִּקְצֹעֹ֖ת יִהְיֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And they will be twins from below, and together they will be complete at its top, to the one ring; so it will be for both of them; for the two corners they will be.
pieces: They are to be double from the bottom and joined together at the top in a single ring. Both corner frames are to be made this way; they will form the two corners.

L.24: And they shall be double from below, and together they shall be complete at its top, to the one ring; so it shall be for both of them; they shall be for the two corners.

R.24: These corner frames must be double, joined together from bottom to top and held at the top by one ring. Make both corners this way.

decisions.choice: twins ... complete: the corner frames are doubled and joined
alternatives: made double from bottom to top
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "twins" from below and "complete" or "whole" at the top. It seems each corner frame was paired with the next frame, or made double, and joined at the top by a ring, to make the corner strong. How this was done is not clear.

decisions.choice: the one ring: a single ring at the top
decisions.reason: A ring held the paired frames together at the top. It may be the ring for the top crossbar (verse 29).

records.source: וְהָיוּ֙ שְׁמֹנָ֣ה קְרָשִׁ֔ים וְאַדְנֵיהֶ֣ם כֶּ֔סֶף שִׁשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר אֲדָנִ֑ים שְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת הַקֶּ֣רֶשׁ הָאֶחָ֔ד וּשְׁנֵ֣י אֲדָנִ֔ים תַּ֖חַת הַקֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָאֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And they will be eight frames, and their bases [of] silver, sixteen bases: two bases under the one frame and two bases under the one frame.
pieces: The back wall will then have eight frames standing on sixteen silver bases, a pair beneath every frame.

L.25: And there shall be eight frames, and their bases of silver, sixteen bases: two bases under the one frame and two bases under the one frame.

R.25: That makes eight frames for the back wall, with sixteen silver bases, two under each frame.

decisions.choice: eight frames: the six of the back wall and the two corner frames
decisions.reason: The six frames of verse 22 and the two of verse 23 make eight. With twenty on each side, there are forty-eight frames and ninety-six bases in all; with the four bases of the veil's pillars (verse 32), that makes the hundred silver bases of 38:27.

decisions.choice: The back wall
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say these frames make the back wall.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ בְרִיחִ֖ם עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים חֲמִשָּׁ֕ה לְקַרְשֵׁ֥י צֶֽלַע־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן הָאֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And you will make bars [of] wood of acacia, five for the frames of the side of the tabernacle, the one,
pieces: You are also to make crossbars from acacia wood, five of them for the frames along one side of the tabernacle,

L.26: And you shall make bars [of] acacia wood: five for the frames of the one side of the tabernacle,

R.26: Make crossbars of acacia wood to hold the frames together. Make five for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,

decisions.choice: bars: long poles laid across the frames
decisions.reason: The word means a bar or bolt (as on a city gate, Judges 16:3). These bars ran sideways through rings on the frames (verse 29) and held each wall in one line.

decisions.choice: crossbars
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "crossbars" to show that the bars run across the frames. Literal keeps "bars". Readable also adds what they are for.

records.source: וַחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה בְרִיחִ֔ם לְקַרְשֵׁ֥י צֶֽלַע־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן הַשֵּׁנִ֑ית וַחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה בְרִיחִ֗ם לְקַרְשֵׁי֙ צֶ֣לַע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֔ן לַיַּרְכָתַ֖יִם יָֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: and five bars for the frames of the side of the tabernacle, the second, and five bars for the frames of the side of the tabernacle, for the far parts, seaward.
pieces: five for the frames of its other side, and five for the frames of the rear wall facing west.

L.27: and five bars for the frames of the second side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the frames of the side of the tabernacle at the rear, westward.

R.27: five for the other side, and five for the back wall on the west.

decisions.choice: five bars on each of the three walls: fifteen in all
decisions.reason: Each of the three walls had five bars; the east end was the entrance, with its own screen and pillars (verses 36-37). Verse 28 describes the middle bar of each wall.

records.source: וְהַבְּרִ֥יחַ הַתִּיכֹ֖ן בְּת֣וֹךְ הַקְּרָשִׁ֑ים מַבְרִ֕חַ מִן־הַקָּצֶ֖ה אֶל־הַקָּצֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And the middle bar in the midst of the frames [will be] passing through from the end to the end.
pieces: The middle crossbar, set halfway up the frames, is to reach all the way from one end to the other.

L.28: And the middle bar, in the midst of the frames, shall pass through from end to end.

R.28: The middle crossbar must go halfway up the frames and reach from one end of the wall to the other.

decisions.choice: the middle bar passes from end to end: one bar running the whole length of the wall
decisions.reason: The middle bar reaches the full length of each wall; the other four are perhaps shorter, two above and two below it. "In the midst of the frames" may mean halfway up, or that the bar ran through the frames themselves; the word "pass through" is used of it again in 36:33.

records.source: וְֽאֶת־הַקְּרָשִׁ֞ים תְּצַפֶּ֣ה זָהָ֗ב וְאֶת־טַבְּעֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה זָהָ֔ב בָּתִּ֖ים לַבְּרִיחִ֑ם וְצִפִּיתָ֥ אֶת־הַבְּרִיחִ֖ם זָהָֽב׃
records.gloss: And the frames you will overlay [with] gold, and their rings you will make [of] gold, houses for the bars, and you will overlay the bars [with] gold.
pieces: Overlay the frames with gold, and make their rings of gold as holders for the crossbars; the crossbars too you are to overlay with gold.

L.29: And the frames you shall overlay [with] gold, and their rings you shall make [of] gold, holders for the bars; and you shall overlay the bars [with] gold.

R.29: Cover the frames and the crossbars with gold. Then make gold rings on the frames. The crossbars will slide through these rings.

decisions.choice: houses for the bars: holders for the bars
decisions.reason: The Hebrew calls the rings "houses" for the bars: they are where the bars rest. The same phrase is used of the rings for the poles of the ark and table (25:27).

decisions.choice: overlay: cover with a layer of gold
decisions.reason: The verb means to cover or plate. The wood was covered with thin sheets of gold, as the ark was (25:11).

records.source: וַהֲקֵמֹתָ֖ אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּ֑ן כְּמִ֨שְׁפָּט֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרְאֵ֖יתָ בָּהָֽר׃ס
records.gloss: And you will set up the tabernacle according to its plan which you have been shown on the mountain.
pieces: Erect the tabernacle following the design that was shown to you on the mountain.

L.30: And you shall set up the tabernacle according to its plan that you were shown on the mountain.

R.30: Set up the tabernacle just as I showed you on the mountain.

decisions.choice: its plan: the right arrangement laid down for it
decisions.reason: The word usually means a judgment or a rule; here it is the proper order or design of the tabernacle. Elsewhere the word for "pattern" is used (25:9, 40).

decisions.choice: shown on the mountain: God showed Moses the design on Sinai
decisions.reason: As in 25:9, 40 and 27:8, the tabernacle is built after what God showed Moses on the mountain. Hebrews 8:5 quotes 25:40 and calls the earthly sanctuary a copy and shadow of the heavenly one.

decisions.choice: I showed you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "you were shown". God is speaking, and he is the one who showed Moses, so Readable says "I showed you".

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ פָרֹ֗כֶת תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֑ר מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חֹשֵׁ֛ב יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָ֖הּ כְּרֻבִֽים׃
records.gloss: And you will make a veil [of] blue and purple and scarlet [yarn] and fine twisted linen; the work of a skillful worker one will make it, [with] cherubim.
pieces: Make the inner curtain of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen. It is to be the work of a skilled craftsman, with cherubim worked into its design.

L.31: And you shall make a veil of blue and purple and scarlet [yarn] and fine twisted linen; the work of a skilled craftsman, one shall make it [with] cherubim.

R.31: Make an inner curtain from blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen. Have a skilled craftsman work cherubim into it.

decisions.choice: veil: the dividing curtain before the most holy place
decisions.reason: This word is used only of the curtain that shut off the most holy place (verse 33; Leviticus 16:2). In the temple, the veil was torn in two at the death of Jesus (Matthew 27:51; Hebrews 10:20).

decisions.choice: the work of a skillful worker, with cherubim: like the linen curtains
decisions.reason: The veil is made of the same materials and with the same woven cherubim as the inner curtains of the tabernacle (verse 1). Cherubim guarded the way to the tree of life (Genesis 3:24), and two cherubim stood over the ark (25:18-22).

decisions.choice: inner curtain / curtain
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "veil", the traditional name for this hanging. Balanced and Readable say "curtain", and "inner curtain" the first time, to set it apart from the curtains of verses 1-13.

records.heading: The inner curtain and the screen

records.source: וְנָתַתָּ֣ה אֹתָ֗הּ עַל־אַרְבָּעָה֙ עַמּוּדֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים מְצֻפִּ֣ים זָהָ֔ב וָוֵיהֶ֖ם זָהָ֑ב עַל־אַרְבָּעָ֖ה אַדְנֵי־כָֽסֶף׃
records.gloss: And you will put it on four pillars of acacia overlaid [with] gold, their hooks [of] gold, on four bases of silver.
pieces: Hang it from four pillars of acacia overlaid with gold. Their hooks are to be of gold, and they will stand on four bases of silver.

L.32: And you shall hang it on four pillars of acacia overlaid [with] gold, their hooks [of] gold, on four bases of silver.

R.32: Hang it on four acacia-wood posts covered with gold. Give the posts gold hooks and set them in four silver bases.

decisions.choice: hooks: pegs or hooks on the pillars
decisions.reason: The word is used only of the hooks or pegs on the tabernacle's pillars (here, verse 37; 27:10). The veil hung from them.

decisions.choice: posts
decisions.reason: Readable says "posts" for the pillars, since they are wooden poles, not stone columns.

records.source: וְנָתַתָּ֣ה אֶת־הַפָּרֹכֶת֮ תַּ֣חַת הַקְּרָסִים֒ וְהֵבֵאתָ֥ שָׁ֨מָּה֙ מִבֵּ֣ית לַפָּרֹ֔כֶת אֵ֖ת אֲר֣וֹן הָעֵד֑וּת וְהִבְדִּילָ֤ה הַפָּרֹ֨כֶת֙ לָכֶ֔ם בֵּ֣ין הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ וּבֵ֖ין קֹ֥דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And you will put the veil under the clasps, and you will bring there, inside the veil, the ark of the testimony; and the veil will separate for you between the holy [place] and the holy of holies.
pieces: Put the curtain in place beneath the clasps, and bring the ark of the testimony there, inside the curtain. For you it will mark the division between the holy place and the most holy place.

L.33: And you shall put the veil under the clasps, and you shall bring there, inside the veil, the ark of the testimony; and the veil shall separate for you between the holy [place] and the holy of holies.

R.33: Hang the inner curtain below the clasps. Then bring the ark that holds the covenant tablets in behind it. This curtain will divide the holy place from the most holy place.

decisions.choice: under the clasps: below the line where the two sets of linen curtains meet
decisions.reason: The gold clasps of verse 6 joined the two sets of five linen curtains, 20 cubits from the front. Hanging the veil below them would make the most holy place a cube of 10 cubits each way. The verse does not give this measure; it follows from the earlier ones.

decisions.choice: the testimony: the tablets of the covenant
decisions.reason: "The testimony" is the two stone tablets that God gave and told Moses to put in the ark (25:16, 21; 31:18), so the ark is named after them.

decisions.choice: the holy of holies: the most holy place
decisions.reason: "Holy of holies" is the Hebrew way of saying "most holy", as "king of kings" means the greatest king. The inner room was holier than the outer one, called simply "the holy place".

decisions.choice: the ark that holds the covenant tablets
decisions.reason: Readable calls the ark of the testimony "the ark that holds the covenant tablets", since "the testimony" is the tablets of the covenant kept inside it.

records.source: וְנָתַתָּ֙ אֶת־הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת עַ֖ל אֲר֣וֹן הָעֵדֻ֑ת בְּקֹ֖דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And you will put the atonement cover on the ark of the testimony in the holy of holies.
pieces: Place the mercy seat on the ark of the testimony in the most holy place.

L.34: And you shall put the mercy seat on the ark of the testimony in the holy of holies.

R.34: In the most holy place, put the lid of the ark, the place where sins are covered, on the ark that holds the covenant tablets.

decisions.choice: mercy seat: the lid of the ark, the place of atonement
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb for making atonement, covering sin. It is the gold lid of the ark (25:17-22), where the blood was sprinkled on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:14-15). See the note at 25:17.

decisions.choice: the lid of the ark, the place where sins are covered
decisions.reason: Readable explains the mercy seat by what it is and what it was for, as at 25:17. Literal and Balanced keep "mercy seat".

records.source: וְשַׂמְתָּ֤ אֶת־הַשֻּׁלְחָן֙ מִח֣וּץ לַפָּרֹ֔כֶת וְאֶת־הַמְּנֹרָה֙ נֹ֣כַח הַשֻּׁלְחָ֔ן עַ֛ל צֶ֥לַע הַמִּשְׁכָּ֖ן תֵּימָ֑נָה וְהַ֨שֻּׁלְחָ֔ן תִּתֵּ֖ן עַל־צֶ֥לַע צָפֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And you will set the table outside the veil, and the lampstand opposite the table on the side of the tabernacle southward, and the table you will put on the north side.
pieces: Set the table outside the curtain, and the lampstand opposite the table, on the south side of the tabernacle. The table you are to put on the north side.

L.35: And you shall set the table outside the veil, and the lampstand opposite the table, on the side of the tabernacle toward the south; and the table you shall put on the north side.

R.35: Put the table and the lampstand outside the inner curtain. Put the lampstand on the south side, across from the table. Put the table on the north side.

decisions.choice: the table and the lampstand: the furnishings of the holy place
decisions.reason: The table for the bread of the Presence (25:23-30) and the lampstand (25:31-40) stand in the outer room, outside the veil. The altar of incense is added in 30:1-6, in front of the veil.

decisions.choice: southward ... north: the lampstand on the left of the one entering, the table on the right
decisions.reason: Coming in from the east, the lampstand stood on the south side, on the left, and the table on the north side, on the right.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֤יתָ מָסָךְ֙ לְפֶ֣תַח הָאֹ֔הֶל תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן וְתוֹלַ֥עַת שָׁנִ֖י וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֑ר מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה רֹקֵֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will make a screen for the entrance of the tent [of] blue and purple and scarlet [yarn] and fine twisted linen, the work of a worker in colors.
pieces: Make a screen for the doorway of the tent from blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, worked in colors by an embroiderer.

L.36: And you shall make a screen for the entrance of the tent [of] blue and purple and scarlet [yarn] and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer.

R.36: Make a screen for the entrance of the tent. Make it from blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, and have an embroiderer decorate it.

decisions.choice: screen: a hanging that covers the entrance
decisions.reason: The word means a covering or screen. It closes the east entrance of the tent and is different from the veil inside (verse 31). The courtyard gate has a screen of its own (27:16).

decisions.choice: the work of a worker in colors: embroidered or woven in colored patterns
alternatives: the work of a weaver of colors
decisions.reason: The worker named here works in many colors, by needle or on the loom. This is a different craft from the "skillful worker" whose cloth bears cherubim (verses 1 and 31); no cherubim are named on the screen.

records.source: וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לַמָּסָ֗ךְ חֲמִשָּׁה֙ עַמּוּדֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֔ים וְצִפִּיתָ֤ אֹתָם֙ זָהָ֔ב וָוֵיהֶ֖ם זָהָ֑ב וְיָצַקְתָּ֣ לָהֶ֔ם חֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אַדְנֵ֥י נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃ס
records.gloss: And you will make for the screen five pillars of acacia and overlay them [with] gold, their hooks [of] gold, and you will cast for them five bases of bronze.
pieces: Make five pillars of acacia wood for the screen and overlay them with gold; their hooks are to be gold. Cast five bases of bronze for them as well.

L.37: And you shall make for the screen five pillars of acacia and overlay them [with] gold, their hooks [of] gold; and you shall cast for them five bases of bronze.

R.37: Make five acacia-wood posts for the screen. Cover them with gold and give them gold hooks. Then pour melted bronze into molds to make five bases for them.

decisions.choice: bases of bronze: a less costly metal at the entrance
decisions.reason: Inside, the frames and the pillars of the veil stand on silver (verses 19 and 32); the pillars of the entrance stand on bronze, as do those of the courtyard (27:10). The metals are less precious the farther they are from the most holy place.

decisions.choice: pour melted bronze into molds
decisions.reason: Readable explains "cast". It says "posts" for the pillars, as in verse 32.
